# Stage 3: the core screens and journeys

The core screens, so a person can do every core journey: check in, read a goal, see what needs attention, run a review.

**Today:** an outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand, with no drill yet. A rebuild can start from it; proving it is done is by hand until it has a drill.

## Entry criteria

- Stage 2 passes its exit criteria.

## What to read

- [The screens](../core/screens.md): each core route, its purpose, named parts and one main action.
- [The journeys](../core/journeys.md): what people do end to end, the most steps each may take, and the ease test.
- [The requirements](../core/requirements.md): each one, with the screens and Help article that cover it.
- [The vocabulary](../core/vocabulary.md): where each word may appear. A status is always a shape and a word.

## What to build

- Each core screen at its route, with its named parts and one main action at a time.
- Every core journey, within its step budget, on a phone (390px) and a desktop (1440px).
- A goal’s page in one order at every width: the summary and its buttons, Next steps and asks, Why, the chart, then the rest. Its main button is a rule of who is looking ([acting on a goal](../core/rules/goal-act.md)), not a layout choice; Next steps and asks is one query over the goal’s asks and next steps; someone acting for the owner (R6b) presses the owner’s buttons for them.
- One find-and-pick control wherever a person, team or goal is chosen (requirement `FIND-AND-PICK`): the choice in words with Change, suggestions before typing ([finding things](../core/rules/finding.md), rule 6), then a search through the `Search` port, its count, at most 50 rows, arrow keys, Enter and Escape. Never a list of everyone: the server’s search plugs in behind the port.
- Find from anywhere (requirement `FIND-ANYWHERE`): the sidebar’s Find, the phone’s Find button and Ctrl K (Cmd K) open one search across goals, people, teams and a module’s kinds, drawn in groups of three with “See all {n} {things}”, a key’s goal alone and first, and Enter opening the first row ([finding things](../core/rules/finding.md), rule 8). Each group is one call to the `Search` port, so the server’s search answers it.
- One list bar on every list (requirement `LIST-BAR`): the search, then the count line, the filter line and what found nothing in [finding things](../core/rules/finding.md)’ words; the list’s search and filters in the address, a choice adding a history entry. The server pages the list (R4).
- The menu, the lit item and a page’s name as three rules of the viewer and the address ([navigation](../core/rules/navigation.md)), drawn by the shell: a module adds a menu item in a group, names its pages from their thing, and fills places on a goal’s, a person’s and a team’s page.
- Where you are (requirements `NAV-WHERE`, `NAV-BACK`, `NAV-FORMS`): the browser’s title is the page’s own name by rule 2; one back link per page by rule 4, which goes back in the tab’s history (stepping over forms) so it agrees with the browser’s Back, and up to the parent when there is no history; a form’s one closing control in words, asking first before throwing typed words away.
- New goal and the first check-in keep day one honest ([a goal not born late](../core/rules/not-born-late.md)): a stage already past is asked about and, if done, recorded done in its own week; a first number off the plan may restart it. These are rules, with the status rules, not screen details.
- New goal in four steps, each an address ([New goal](../core/rules/new-goal.md)): what, who and where, how it’s measured, check. Its level and the suggestions for what it feeds are rules. In the internal app New goal becomes R6c’s draft-and-propose, and owners and teams come from the directory (R2).
- Its last step is the read-back ([the read-back](../core/rules/read-back.md)): the goal in sentences (What, Who and where, Measured by, Left as usual, You said), each with Change to its step and Continue straight back, then “After you publish”: the first check-in’s day, who sees it, the reviews it joins (`reviewsJoining`) and how long it can be taken back. A rule, so the internal app’s form and its draft-and-propose say the same.
- One set of rules at every door ([goal entry](../core/rules/goal-entry.md)): New goal, the edit page, set-up’s goal cards, a spreadsheet’s Goals rows and the AI tools ask the same `goalMustFix`, in the same words, and the form saves through the `saveGoal` command, never by itself, so nothing the change engine would refuse is saved. Anyone may add a goal for anyone at any level; only its owner or an admin changes it. The questions (`goalChecks`, rule 3) are asked the same way: possible but unlikely values (over 100%, below zero, a hundredfold, a billion, no unit, a wide margin, a late hand-set plan, the same name in the same team, an owner in another team, a link to a lower level, a stage already past) are a Check under their field, answered once for the values they are about and kept in History as Checked; Continue and the save wait for them, and the AI tools list them and take `confirm`. Both belong with the status rules in stage 1’s conformance data; until then the change engine’s cases in `import.csv` carry them (`has-words`, `same-as-start`, `stage-twice`, a goal added for someone else, `over-100-and-hundredfold`, `margin-wide`, `feeds-lower`).
- A goal’s weeks are picked, never typed (requirement `GOAL-DATES`; [years and weeks](../core/rules/years-and-weeks.md)): a number goal’s Baseline with its From and Target with its To, and a stage’s Due, each chosen from a short list of a goal year’s weeks with their dates, opened at the chosen week, with up to three named weeks. The data keeps weeks counted from the cycle’s start; one rule converts, and the sheet and the AI tools write `2026-W46`. A plan whose From is still to come is not due until then. The change engine’s cases in `import.csv` carry the sheet’s side (`to-before-from`, `week-unknown`, `from-pair-disagrees`, `to-next-year`).
- Change a goal is one page (requirement `GOAL-EDIT-PAGE`): four sections an address opens at (`#definition`, `#plan`, `#owner`, then More details), its one closing control “Close and keep the draft”, Save changes held at the window’s foot, and old `?part=` links led to the matching section. A plan change after check-ins have started needs a reason; that is the plan-change rule, not the page’s.

## Exit criteria

1. Each core journey in [the journeys](../core/journeys.md) can be done within its budget, by hand, on both widths.
2. Each core requirement in [the requirements](../core/requirements.md) holds.
3. No screen offers a person, team or goal from a list of everything (Faro checks it with `scripts/check-pickers.mjs`; the places it still allows are listed in `scripts/pickers-left.json`).

## Gaps in the kit

Where the kit doesn’t yet hold what this stage needs, so a rebuild would have to guess:

- The journeys are driven by Faro’s own eval scripts against Faro’s own markup (`evals/journeys.cjs`), which are not in the kit and would not run against another build. There is no portable journey runner yet.
- The design rules (`docs/design-rules.md`) and the look are not in the kit; a heading or button whose words are worked out when it shows isn’t listed (the screens page says so).
- The Help guide’s articles are summarised on the screens page, not given in full.
- Faro’s mark (the F’s stem, beam and bar, and “aro”) is drawn from paths in `src/ui/brandPaths.ts`, which are not in the kit: the home-screen icon and the launch splash (requirement `LAUNCH`) are described in words, so a rebuild draws its own mark to them.
